title: Request for a hearing on a licence denial based on a conviction (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 485, 480, 482)
summary: Sections 480 and 482 set the rules a California licensing board follows before it denies a licence because of a conviction. They do not create a request of their own. The request the law provides is the written request for a hearing under § 485(b), made within 60 days after the notice of denial is served. In that request the applicant can rely on §§ 480 and 482 and send evidence of rehabilitation under § 481(c).
scope: For a licence regulated by the Business and Professions Code, after a board serves a notice of denial under § 485(b). Not for licences under the State Bar Act (Chapter 4 of Division 3), the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act (Division 9) or the Gambling Control Act (Chapter 5 of Division 8): § 476(a) says Division 1.5, which holds §§ 480 to 487, does not apply to them, so this draft does not apply to them either. Section 480(i) leaves the licensing authority of the State Athletic Commission, the Bureau for Private Postsecondary Education and the California Horse Racing Board unchanged. Some practice acts and divisions have conviction rules of their own. The Board of Pharmacy may deny “Notwithstanding Section 480” (§ 4202.6). The Board of Accountancy has grounds “In addition to” those of § 480, with no seven-year limit for some financial felonies (§ 5100.2). Three sections direct a board to deny a licence to a person subject to sex-offender registration under Penal Code § 290, with exceptions (§§ 1687, 1958.1, 2660.5). Section 4989.24, in the Educational Psychologist Practice Act, bars a licence for a conviction, in California, in another state or in a territory of the United States, of a crime involving sexual abuse of children, or for a person subject to that registration or the equivalent in another state or territory, and its subdivision (b) applies the conditions for denial in § 480 to such a denial. For a state cannabis licence under Division 10, § 26057(b)(2) lets the Department of Cannabis Control deny for conduct that is a ground for denial under Chapter 2 of Division 1.5 (commencing with § 480), “except as otherwise specified” in § 26057 and § 26059. Read the practice act or division that governs your licence. This draft is not for licences under other codes.

letter.subject: Request for hearing on the denial of my license application

elements.label: Date you send it
elements.quote: if written request for hearing is made within 60 days after service of the notice of denial
elements.help: The 60 days for the request run from service of the notice of denial, so keep a record of when and how you sent it.

elements.label: You
elements.quote: by registered mail addressed to the applicant at the latest address filed by the applicant in writing with the board in his or her application or otherwise
elements.help: The law lets the board serve the notice of denial by registered mail at the latest address you filed with it in writing. This letter gives your current address in writing.

elements.label: The board that denied the licence
elements.quote: Upon denial of an application for a license under this chapter or Section 496, the board shall do either of the following

fields.name: board
fields.label: Board, bureau or other agency that denied the licence

fields.name: board_address
fields.label: Its address, from the notice of denial (optional)

elements.help: Send the request to the board that denied the application, at the address on its notice. The statute does not ask for the address; it is there so the letter can be sent.

elements.label: The application that was denied
elements.quote: Notify the applicant that the application is denied, stating (1) the reason for the denial

fields.name: application_no
fields.label: Application or reference number on the notice (optional)

elements.help: The notice of denial states the reason for the denial. Copy the licence and any reference number from it.

elements.label: When the notice was mailed or served
elements.quote: Service by mail is complete on the date of mailing.

fields.name: notice_date
fields.label: Date the notice of denial was mailed or served (optional)

elements.letter: The notice of denial was mailed or served on {notice_date}.
elements.help: The 60 days run from service. When the notice is mailed, service is complete on the date of mailing, not the day it arrives.

elements.label: Ask for a hearing, in writing
elements.quote: Unless written request for hearing is made within the 60-day period, the applicant’s right to a hearing is deemed waived.
elements.letter: I request a hearing on the denial of my application.
elements.help: Send the request in writing within 60 days after service of the notice of denial. Without a timely written request the right to a hearing is waived.

elements.label: The conviction was dismissed
elements.quote: a person shall not be denied a license on the basis of any conviction, or on the basis of the acts underlying the conviction, that has been dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, 1203.42, or 1203.425 of the Penal Code, or a comparable dismissal or expungement

fields.name: dismissal_detail
fields.label: Penal Code section, court and case number
fields.placeholder: e.g. Penal Code § 1203.4, Superior Court of ... County, case no. ...

elements.help: The Judicial Council's petition for a dismissal under Penal Code § 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41 or 1203.42 is CR-180, and CR-181 is the order. They are court forms for getting the dismissal, not forms for this letter.

forms.title: Petition for Dismissal
forms.notes: Relief needs 15 days' notice to the prosecuting attorney (§ 1203.4(d)). No fee is stated on the form.
forms.role: What it is: the Judicial Council's petition to the court for a dismissal under Penal Code § 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41 or 1203.42.

forms.title: Order for Dismissal
forms.role: What it is: the Judicial Council's order for that dismissal, filed with the petition.

elements.label: Proof of the dismissal
elements.quote: An applicant who has a conviction that has been dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, or 1203.42 of the Penal Code shall provide proof of the dismissal if it is not reflected on the report furnished by the Department of Justice.

fields.name: proof_enclosed
fields.label: I enclose proof of the dismissal

elements.letter: I enclose proof of the dismissal.
elements.help: The statute does not say what counts as proof.
elements.condition: Only for a dismissal under Penal Code § 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41 or 1203.42 that is not on the Department of Justice report.

elements.label: Certificate of rehabilitation, pardon or rehabilitation
elements.quote: a person shall not be denied a license on the basis that the person has been convicted of a crime, or on the basis of acts underlying a conviction for a crime, if that person has obtained a certificate of rehabilitation under Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 4852.01) of Title 6 of Part 3 of the Penal Code, has been granted clemency or a pardon by a state or federal executive, or has made a showing of rehabilitation pursuant to Section 482

fields.name: rehab_basis
fields.label: Which applies
options: I have obtained a certificate of rehabilitation
I have been granted clemency or a pardon by a state or federal executive
I have made a showing of rehabilitation under Section 482

elements.label: Sentence completed without a violation
elements.quote: Each board shall consider whether an applicant or licensee has made a showing of rehabilitation if either of the following are met: (1) The applicant or licensee has completed the criminal sentence at issue without a violation of parole or probation.

fields.name: sentence_completed
fields.label: I completed the sentence without a violation of parole or probation

elements.letter: I completed the criminal sentence at issue without a violation of parole or probation, and I ask the board to consider whether I have made a showing of rehabilitation ({cite}: “{quote}”).
elements.help: When this is true, § 482(b) directs the board to consider whether you showed rehabilitation; it does not direct the board to find that you did.

elements.label: The seven-year condition
elements.quote: The applicant has been convicted of a crime within the preceding seven years from the date of application that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the application is made, regardless of whether the applicant was incarcerated for that crime, or the applicant has been convicted of a crime that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the application is made and for which the applicant is presently incarcerated or for which the applicant was released from incarceration within the preceding seven years from the date of application

fields.name: seven_years_facts
fields.label: Your facts on the seven-year condition (optional)
fields.placeholder: e.g. the date of the conviction; whether you were incarcerated for it and, if so, the date of your release; the date you applied

elements.letter: Under § 480(a), a board may deny a license on the ground of a conviction or of formal discipline only if one of two conditions is met. The first, in {cite}, subject to the exceptions in its subparagraphs (A) and (B), reads: “{quote}.” My facts on this condition: {seven_years_facts}
elements.help: Give your own facts. The draft does not say whether the condition is met. The condition has two branches: a conviction within the seven years, or a conviction for which the applicant is incarcerated now or was released from incarceration within the seven years. The seven-year limit does not apply in the situations in § 480(a)(1)(A) and (B) (see the notes), and some practice acts have rules of their own (see the scope above).

elements.label: An arrest without a conviction
elements.quote: a board shall not deny a license on the basis of an arrest that resulted in a disposition other than a conviction, including an arrest that resulted in an infraction, citation, or a juvenile adjudication

fields.name: arrest_only
fields.label: Part of the denial rests on an arrest that did not end in a conviction

elements.letter: Part of the denial rests on an arrest that did not result in a conviction. Under {cite}, “{quote}.”

elements.label: Evidence of rehabilitation
elements.quote: A board shall not deny a license based in whole or in part on a conviction without considering evidence of rehabilitation submitted by an applicant pursuant to any process established in the practice act or regulations of the particular board and as directed by Section 482.

fields.name: evidence_list
fields.label: Evidence you enclose (optional)
fields.placeholder: e.g. certificate of completion of a training programme; letter from an employer

elements.letter:
I enclose the following evidence of rehabilitation and ask the board to consider it:
{evidence_list}
elements.help: Each board sets its own process for evidence, in its practice act or regulations. Check the board's rules. There is no statewide evidence form; the form linked here is about your own record.

elements.label: Licences outside this draft
elements.quote: Except as provided in subdivision (b), nothing in this division shall apply to the licensure or registration of persons pursuant to Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 6000) of Division 3, or pursuant to Division 9 (commencing with Section 23000) or pursuant to Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 19800) of Division 8.
elements.help: Division 1.5 of the Business and Professions Code, which holds §§ 480 to 487, does not apply to licences under the State Bar Act (Chapter 4 of Division 3), the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act (Division 9) or the Gambling Control Act (Chapter 5 of Division 8). This draft does not apply to those licences. Under subdivision (b), § 494.5 still applies to them.

elements.label: Three bodies keep their own rules
elements.quote: This section does not in any way modify or otherwise affect the existing authority of the following entities in regard to licensure: (1) The State Athletic Commission. (2) The Bureau for Private Postsecondary Education. (3) The California Horse Racing Board.
elements.help: Section 480 leaves the licensing authority of these three bodies unchanged.

elements.label: If the board served a statement of issues instead
elements.quote: File and serve a statement of issues in accordance with Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 11500) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code.
elements.help: This draft is for a notice of denial under § 485(b). If the board instead filed and served a statement of issues under § 485(a), the Government Code procedure for that applies, and this letter may not be the right step.

elements.label: When a board may deny for a conviction
elements.quote: a board may deny a license regulated by this code on the grounds that the applicant has been convicted of a crime or has been subject to formal discipline only if either of the following conditions are met
elements.help: Section 480(a) lists two conditions. (1) A substantially related conviction within the seven years before the application, or a substantially related conviction for which the applicant is incarcerated now or was released from incarceration within those seven years; subparagraphs (A) and (B) lift the seven-year limit for some crimes. (2) Formal discipline by a licensing board in or outside California within those seven years, for substantially related professional misconduct that would have been cause for discipline before the board. Paragraph (2) has two qualifiers. Discipline within the seven years is not a basis for denial if it was based on a conviction dismissed under Penal Code § 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, 1203.42 or 1203.425, or a comparable dismissal or expungement. Discipline older than seven years can be a ground only if it was for conduct that, by a California physician and surgeon, would have been sexual abuse, misconduct or relations with a patient under § 726, or sexual exploitation under § 729(a). Some practice acts have rules of their own (see the scope above).

elements.label: Exceptions to the seven-year limit
elements.quote: However, the preceding seven-year limitation shall not apply in either of the following situations: (A) The applicant was convicted of a serious felony, as defined in Section 1192.7 of the Penal Code or a crime for which registration is required pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of subdivision (d) of Section 290 of the Penal Code. (B) The applicant was convicted of a financial crime currently classified as a felony that is directly and adversely related to the fiduciary qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the application is made, pursuant to regulations adopted by the board, and for which the applicant is seeking licensure under any of the following: (i) Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 6500) of Division 3. (ii) Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3. (iii) Chapter 11.3 (commencing with Section 7512) of Division 3. (iv) Licensure as a funeral director or cemetery manager under Chapter 12 (commencing with Section 7600) of Division 3. (v) Division 4 (commencing with Section 10000).
elements.help: The seven-year limit does not apply to (A) a serious felony under Penal Code § 1192.7 or a crime that carries sex-offender registration under Penal Code § 290(d)(2) or (3), or (B) for the licences listed in (i) to (v), a felony financial crime directly and adversely related to the licence's fiduciary qualifications, functions or duties, under the board's regulations.

elements.label: Formal discipline as a ground for denial
elements.quote: The applicant has been subjected to formal discipline by a licensing board in or outside California within the preceding seven years from the date of application based on professional misconduct that would have been cause for discipline before the board for which the present application is made and that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the present application is made. However, prior disciplinary action by a licensing board within the preceding seven years shall not be the basis for denial of a license if the basis for that disciplinary action was a conviction that has been dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, 1203.42, or 1203.425 of the Penal Code or a comparable dismissal or expungement. Formal discipline that occurred earlier than seven years preceding the date of application may be grounds for denial of a license only if the formal discipline was for conduct that, if committed in this state by a physician and surgeon licensed pursuant to Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 2000) of Division 2, would have constituted an act of sexual abuse, misconduct, or relations with a patient pursuant to Section 726 or sexual exploitation as defined in subdivision (a) of Section 729.
elements.help: The second condition of § 480(a), quoted in full with both qualifiers: discipline based on a dismissed conviction is not a basis for denial, and discipline older than seven years counts only for the conduct named in the last sentence.

elements.label: What the board's criteria for a substantially related crime include
elements.quote: Criteria for determining whether a crime is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession a board regulates shall include all of the following: (1) The nature and gravity of the offense. (2) The number of years elapsed since the date of the offense. (3) The nature and duties of the profession in which the applicant seeks licensure or in which the licensee is licensed.
elements.help: The board's criteria for whether a crime is substantially related to the licence include the nature and gravity of the offense, the years since the offense, and the nature and duties of the profession.

elements.level_label: What the other side has to do
elements.label: What the board shall put in the notice of denial
elements.quote: If a board decides to deny an application for licensure based solely or in part on the applicant’s conviction history, the board shall notify the applicant in writing of all of the following: (A) The denial or disqualification of licensure. (B) Any existing procedure the board has for the applicant to challenge the decision or to request reconsideration. (C) That the applicant has the right to appeal the board’s decision.
elements.help: Read the notice for the board's own challenge or reconsideration procedure.

elements.label: A copy of your own conviction history
elements.quote: The processes for the applicant to request a copy of the applicant’s complete conviction history and question the accuracy or completeness of the record pursuant to Sections 11122 to 11127 of the Penal Code.
elements.help: Section 480(f)(3)(D) puts this in the notice of denial too. The Department of Justice's form for requesting a copy of your own record is BCIA 8016RR.

elements.level_label: What the other side has to do
elements.label: When the board holds the hearing
elements.quote: If a hearing is requested by the applicant, the board shall conduct such hearing within 90 days from the date the hearing is requested unless the applicant shall request or agree in writing to a postponement or continuance of the hearing. Notwithstanding the above, the Office of Administrative Hearings may order, or on a showing of good cause, grant a request for, up to 45 additional days within which to conduct a hearing, except in cases involving alleged examination or licensing fraud, in which cases the period may be up to 180 days. In no case shall more than two such orders be made or requests be granted.
elements.help: The 90 days run from the date of your request, unless you ask for or agree in writing to a postponement or continuance. The Office of Administrative Hearings may add up to 45 days (up to 180 in cases of alleged examination or licensing fraud), with no more than two such orders or grants.

elements.label: Reapplying
elements.quote: The earliest date on which the applicant may reapply for a license which shall be one year from the effective date of the decision, or service of the notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, unless the board prescribes an earlier date or a later date is prescribed by another statute.
elements.help: The decision or notice states the earliest date you may reapply.

elements.label: Evidence when you reapply
elements.quote: That all competent evidence of rehabilitation presented will be considered upon a reapplication.
elements.help: The decision or notice of denial also tells you that all competent evidence of rehabilitation presented will be considered if you reapply.

elements.level_label: What the other side has to do
elements.label: The board serves its rehabilitation criteria with the notice
elements.quote: Along with the decision, or the notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, the board shall serve a copy of the criteria relating to rehabilitation formulated under Section 482.
elements.help: With the decision or the notice of denial, the board serves a copy of its criteria for evaluating rehabilitation (§ 482).

(a) Except as provided in subdivision (b), nothing in this division shall apply to the licensure or registration of persons pursuant to Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 6000) of Division 3, or pursuant to Division 9 (commencing with Section 23000) or pursuant to Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 19800) of Division 8.

(b) Section 494.5 shall apply to the licensure of persons authorized to practice law pursuant to Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 6000) of Division 3, and the licensure or registration of persons pursuant to Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 19800) of Division 8 or pursuant to Division 9 (commencing with Section 23000).

sources.text:
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this code, a board may deny a license regulated by this code on the grounds that the applicant has been convicted of a crime or has been subject to formal discipline only if either of the following conditions are met:

(1) The applicant has been convicted of a crime within the preceding seven years from the date of application that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the application is made, regardless of whether the applicant was incarcerated for that crime, or the applicant has been convicted of a crime that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the application is made and for which the applicant is presently incarcerated or for which the applicant was released from incarceration within the preceding seven years from the date of application. However, the preceding seven-year limitation shall not apply in either of the following situations:

(A) The applicant was convicted of a serious felony, as defined in Section 1192.7 of the Penal Code or a crime for which registration is required pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of subdivision (d) of Section 290 of the Penal Code.

(B) The applicant was convicted of a financial crime currently classified as a felony that is directly and adversely related to the fiduciary qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the application is made, pursuant to regulations adopted by the board, and for which the applicant is seeking licensure under any of the following:

(i) Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 6500) of Division 3.

(ii) Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3.

(iii) Chapter 11.3 (commencing with Section 7512) of Division 3.

(iv) Licensure as a funeral director or cemetery manager under Chapter 12 (commencing with Section 7600) of Division 3.

(v) Division 4 (commencing with Section 10000).

(2) The applicant has been subjected to formal discipline by a licensing board in or outside California within the preceding seven years from the date of application based on professional misconduct that would have been cause for discipline before the board for which the present application is made and that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession for which the present application is made. However, prior disciplinary action by a licensing board within the preceding seven years shall not be the basis for denial of a license if the basis for that disciplinary action was a conviction that has been dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, 1203.42, or 1203.425 of the Penal Code or a comparable dismissal or expungement. Formal discipline that occurred earlier than seven years preceding the date of application may be grounds for denial of a license only if the formal discipline was for conduct that, if committed in this state by a physician and surgeon licensed pursuant to Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 2000) of Division 2, would have constituted an act of sexual abuse, misconduct, or relations with a patient pursuant to Section 726 or sexual exploitation as defined in subdivision (a) of Section 729.

(b) Notwithstanding any other provision of this code, a person shall not be denied a license on the basis that the person has been convicted of a crime, or on the basis of acts underlying a conviction for a crime, if that person has obtained a certificate of rehabilitation under Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 4852.01) of Title 6 of Part 3 of the Penal Code, has been granted clemency or a pardon by a state or federal executive, or has made a showing of rehabilitation pursuant to Section 482.

(c) Notwithstanding any other provision of this code, a person shall not be denied a license on the basis of any conviction, or on the basis of the acts underlying the conviction, that has been dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, 1203.42, or 1203.425 of the Penal Code, or a comparable dismissal or expungement. An applicant who has a conviction that has been dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.41, or 1203.42 of the Penal Code shall provide proof of the dismissal if it is not reflected on the report furnished by the Department of Justice.

(d) Notwithstanding any other provision of this code, a board shall not deny a license on the basis of an arrest that resulted in a disposition other than a conviction, including an arrest that resulted in an infraction, citation, or a juvenile adjudication.

(e) A board may deny a license regulated by this code on the ground that the applicant knowingly made a false statement of fact that is required to be revealed in the application for the license. A board shall not deny a license based solely on an applicant’s failure to disclose a fact that would not have been cause for denial of the license had it been disclosed.

(f) A board shall follow the following procedures in requesting or acting on an applicant’s criminal history information:

(1) A board issuing a license pursuant to Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 5500), Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 5615), Chapter 10 (commencing with Section 7301), Chapter 20 (commencing with Section 9800), or Chapter 20.3 (commencing with Section 9880), of Division 3, or Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 19000) or Chapter 3.1 (commencing with Section 19225) of Division 8 may require applicants for licensure under those chapters to disclose criminal conviction history on an application for licensure.

(2) Except as provided in paragraph (1), a board shall not require an applicant for licensure to disclose any information or documentation regarding the applicant’s criminal history. However, a board may request mitigating information from an applicant regarding the applicant’s criminal history for purposes of determining substantial relation or demonstrating evidence of rehabilitation, provided that the applicant is informed that disclosure is voluntary and that the applicant’s decision not to disclose any information shall not be a factor in a board’s decision to grant or deny an application for licensure.

(3) If a board decides to deny an application for licensure based solely or in part on the applicant’s conviction history, the board shall notify the applicant in writing of all of the following:

(A) The denial or disqualification of licensure.

(B) Any existing procedure the board has for the applicant to challenge the decision or to request reconsideration.

(C) That the applicant has the right to appeal the board’s decision.

(D) The processes for the applicant to request a copy of the applicant’s complete conviction history and question the accuracy or completeness of the record pursuant to Sections 11122 to 11127 of the Penal Code.

(g) (1) For a minimum of three years, each board under this code shall retain application forms and other documents submitted by an applicant, any notice provided to an applicant, all other communications received from and provided to an applicant, and criminal history reports of an applicant.

(2) Each board under this code shall retain the number of applications received for each license and the number of applications requiring inquiries regarding criminal history. In addition, each licensing authority shall retain all of the following information:

(A) The number of applicants with a criminal record who received notice of denial or disqualification of licensure.

(B) The number of applicants with a criminal record who provided evidence of mitigation or rehabilitation.

(C) The number of applicants with a criminal record who appealed any denial or disqualification of licensure.

(D) The final disposition and demographic information, consisting of voluntarily provided information on race or gender, of any applicant described in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C).

(3) (A) Each board under this code shall annually make available to the public through the board’s internet website and through a report submitted to the appropriate policy committees of the Legislature deidentified information collected pursuant to this subdivision. Each board shall ensure confidentiality of the individual applicants.

(B) A report pursuant to subparagraph (A) shall be submitted in compliance with Section 9795 of the Government Code.

(h) “Conviction” as used in this section shall have the same meaning as defined in Section 7.5.

(i) This section does not in any way modify or otherwise affect the existing authority of the following entities in regard to licensure:

(1) The State Athletic Commission.

(2) The Bureau for Private Postsecondary Education.

(3) The California Horse Racing Board.

sources.text:
(a) Each board under this code shall develop criteria to aid it, when considering the denial, suspension, or revocation of a license, to determine whether a crime is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession it regulates.

(b) Criteria for determining whether a crime is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession a board regulates shall include all of the following:

(1) The nature and gravity of the offense.

(2) The number of years elapsed since the date of the offense.

(3) The nature and duties of the profession in which the applicant seeks licensure or in which the licensee is licensed.

(c) A board shall not deny a license based in whole or in part on a conviction without considering evidence of rehabilitation submitted by an applicant pursuant to any process established in the practice act or regulations of the particular board and as directed by Section 482.

(d) Each board shall post on its Internet Web site a summary of the criteria used to consider whether a crime is considered to be substantially related to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the business or profession it regulates consistent with this section.

(e) This section does not in any way modify or otherwise affect the existing authority of the following entities in regard to licensure:

(1) The State Athletic Commission.

(2) The Bureau for Private Postsecondary Education.

(3) The California Horse Racing Board.

(f) This section shall become operative on July 1, 2020.

(a) Each board under this code shall develop criteria to evaluate the rehabilitation of a person when doing either of the following:

(1) Considering the denial of a license by the board under Section 480.

(2) Considering suspension or revocation of a license under Section 490.

(b) Each board shall consider whether an applicant or licensee has made a showing of rehabilitation if either of the following are met:

(1) The applicant or licensee has completed the criminal sentence at issue without a violation of parole or probation.

(2) The board, applying its criteria for rehabilitation, finds that the applicant is rehabilitated.

(c) This section does not in any way modify or otherwise affect the existing authority of the following entities in regard to licensure:

Upon denial of an application for a license under this chapter or Section 496, the board shall do either of the following:

(a) File and serve a statement of issues in accordance with Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 11500) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code.

(b) Notify the applicant that the application is denied, stating (1) the reason for the denial, and (2) that the applicant has the right to a hearing under Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 11500) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code if written request for hearing is made within 60 days after service of the notice of denial. Unless written request for hearing is made within the 60-day period, the applicant’s right to a hearing is deemed waived.

Service of the notice of denial may be made in the manner authorized for service of summons in civil actions, or by registered mail addressed to the applicant at the latest address filed by the applicant in writing with the board in his or her application or otherwise. Service by mail is complete on the date of mailing.

sources.text:
Where the board has denied an application for a license under this chapter or Section 496, it shall, in its decision, or in its notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, inform the applicant of the following:

(a) The earliest date on which the applicant may reapply for a license which shall be one year from the effective date of the decision, or service of the notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, unless the board prescribes an earlier date or a later date is prescribed by another statute.

(b) That all competent evidence of rehabilitation presented will be considered upon a reapplication.

Along with the decision, or the notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, the board shall serve a copy of the criteria relating to rehabilitation formulated under Section 482.

sources.text: If a hearing is requested by the applicant, the board shall conduct such hearing within 90 days from the date the hearing is requested unless the applicant shall request or agree in writing to a postponement or continuance of the hearing. Notwithstanding the above, the Office of Administrative Hearings may order, or on a showing of good cause, grant a request for, up to 45 additional days within which to conduct a hearing, except in cases involving alleged examination or licensing fraud, in which cases the period may be up to 180 days. In no case shall more than two such orders be made or requests be granted.
